Rafael — quick read and suggested play. We're trying to avoid opening litigation exposure but also must protect trade secrets, model weights, and live customer data. Suggested compromise below:

1) Governing law: State of Delaware OR State of California (Redwood prefers California; we'll accept Delaware if they insist on operational speed).

2) Forum / Emergency Relief carveout: All claims shall be resolved by binding arbitration (commercial arbitration administered by JAMS) except that either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction to protect intellectual property, confidential information, or imminent data-security incidents. Any such court action shall be limited to seeking provisional relief and shall not decide the merits of the dispute, which will be submitted to arbitration.

3) Small-claims / de minimis: Consider keeping their $250k arbitration threshold; for anything under that amount, we could agree to small-claims or expedited processes but insist IP/data is excluded from that threshold.

Proposed language you can send to Elena (short):

"Redwood is willing to accept Delaware as the governing law if necessary to reach agreement quickly, but we need an express carveout preserving the right to seek provisional equitable relief (including temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions) in any court to protect our intellectual property, confidential information and to respond to emergency data-security incidents. All other disputes will be resolved by binding arbitration under JAMS, with arbitration being the exclusive remedy for monetary and contract claims."

Rationale: this preserves operational flexibility for Nimbus while protecting our live systems/data. If procurement will not budge on Delaware, we can concede on law but not on the emergency relief carveout.

If you want, I can redline the clause and send back as a clean counter. Marissa — flagging since this sits with commercial terms; Neha — FYI on timing.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — thanks for the redline and the fast turnaround. We want to keep momentum and have a proposed compromise below that should get us to a signature without jeopardizing either party.

Redwood's proposed compromise (we can send a formal redline if helpful):

- Governing law: State of Delaware (Redwood will accept Delaware to expedite procurement)
- Dispute resolution: Binding arbitration administered by JAMS for all monetary and contractual claims, with the parties to select an arbitrator experienced in commercial software agreements
- Emergency equitable relief: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction to protect intellectual property, confidential information, or to address an active data-security incident. Such judicial proceedings are limited to the provisional relief requested and shall not determine the merits of disputes otherwise subject to arbitration.

We believe this keeps things neutral (Delaware) for Nimbus while ensuring both parties can act quickly to protect IP/data. If that sounds acceptable, I can have the legal team send a clean redline today and procurement can route to signature.

Thanks — Rafael
